key_insight: AutoResearch uses an LLM to autonomously iterate on aerospace control training, but only credits improvements that survive strict audit checks against measured seed noise.
engineering_relevance: This provides a reproducible way to search for better spacecraft guidance and control policies while separating real gains from random seed variation.
method: LLM reads the problem description and run history, then proposes one training-script edit per iteration
Each candidate result is validated with seed-noise measurements, reseeded confirmation, and leave-one-out pruning of edits
The same audited loop is tested on rendezvous and keep-out-zone docking benchmarks
evidence_signal: Across both benchmark problems, the audited policies outperform measured seed noise by many standard deviations, and on docking the learned policy remains feasible on every seed while undirected search finds none.
watch_item: The approach depends on accurate seed-noise calibration and careful auditing, so misestimated noise or benchmark-specific tuning could overstate generality.
paper_title: Agentic AutoResearch forSpace Autonomy: An Auditable, LLM-Driven Research Agent for Aerospace Control Problems
